objectives: Reason about shot, thermal, dark-current noise.
Connect SNR to detector + system design.

slides.title: Photodetector families
slides.body:
**Photodetectors** convert optical signals to electrical. Key families:

• **Photodiode (PD)**: p-n or PIN junction; absorbed photon creates electron-hole pair, swept by field. Si (400-1100 nm); InGaAs (900-1700 nm); Ge (800-1700 nm). Response: ~0.5-0.9 A/W (Si); responsivity = ηe/hν.

• **Avalanche photodiode (APD)**: photodiode with internal carrier multiplication via impact ionization. Gain M ~10-100. SNR-improved vs photodiode but adds excess-noise factor. Used in low-light fiber receivers.

• **Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD)**: APD biased above breakdown; single photon triggers avalanche; counts photons. Used in: LIDAR, quantum cryptography, low-light imaging, neuroscience.

• **Photomultiplier tube (PMT)**: photocathode + dynode chain; ~10⁶× gain. Vacuum tube. Used: low-light + fast (~ns) measurement; replaced by SPAD + SiPM in many applications.

• **Silicon photomultiplier (SiPM)**: array of SPADs operated in Geiger mode; sum gives photon count. Compact + cheap. Used: PET imaging, lidar, particle physics.

• **Charge-coupled device (CCD)** + **CMOS image sensor**: arrays of photodiodes. Smartphone cameras, scientific imaging. CMOS dominant since ~2010 for cost + low-power.

• **Bolometers + thermopiles**: thermal detectors; slow; broadband; used for IR + THz.

• **HgCdTe + InSb detectors**: mid-IR (~3-12 µm). Cooled; expensive; military + scientific.

• **Superconducting nanowire single-photon detector (SNSPD)**: highest efficiency (>95%) single-photon detection; needs ~4K cryocooling. Quantum + telecom research.

**Responsivity**: R = (η × e) / (h ν). For Si at 800 nm, η = 90%: R ≈ 0.58 A/W (vs theoretical 0.65 A/W at η=1).

slides.title: Noise sources + the SNR limit
slides.body:
Detector + system noise has 5 main contributions:

• **Shot noise**: discrete photon arrivals (or electron-hole creation). Poisson statistics. RMS current σ_shot = √(2 e I_total Δf), where I = signal + dark current, Δf = bandwidth. Cannot be reduced (fundamental).

• **Thermal (Johnson-Nyquist) noise** in load resistor: σ_thermal = √(4 k_B T Δf / R). Larger R → less thermal noise but slower bandwidth.

• **Dark current**: leakage when no light; thermally generated carriers. Si photodiode: pA-nA at room T. APD: nA at gain.

• **Excess noise** (APD multiplication): excess-noise factor F(M); for M=10 in Si, F ≈ 6.

• **Amplifier noise**: input-referred current noise of TIA (transimpedance amp).

**Noise equivalent power (NEP)**: signal power at which SNR = 1 (in 1 Hz BW). Lower is better. Si photodiode: ~10⁻¹⁴ W/√Hz; SNSPD: ~10⁻¹⁸ W/√Hz.

**SNR**: signal current / total noise. For shot-noise-limited detection of N photons:
  SNR = √N (square-root scaling).

So distinguishing 100 photons from 0: SNR = 10 (excellent). 10,000 photons: SNR = 100. Photon-counting detectors operate in this regime.

**Cryogenic detectors** (SNSPD, TES): reduce thermal noise to negligible; near-shot-noise limited. Used in quantum networking, deep-space optical communication, axion + dark-matter searches.

**Detection-limit hierarchy**:
1. Photon noise (shot): fundamental.
2. Dark current: temperature-reduction helps.
3. Thermal: cooling + good electronics.
4. Amplifier: low-noise design.
5. RIN (relative intensity noise) of source: stabilize laser.

slides.title: Detector applications + selection
slides.body:
Picking the right detector:

**Visible imaging (smartphone, scientific)**:
- CMOS image sensor; back-side illuminated (BSI) → high QE.
- Si quantum efficiency peaks 50-90% at 500-600 nm.
- Recent: stacked-die designs (Sony Exmor); single-pixel-level analog gain.

**Fiber telecom (1300-1550 nm)**:
- PIN photodiodes (Ge, InGaAs).
- APDs for low-light (long-reach receivers).
- 100G+ coherent: balanced photodiodes + 90° hybrid + 100 GS/s ADCs.

**LIDAR (autonomous vehicles, geomatics)**:
- SPAD/SiPM at 905 nm (Si) or 1550 nm (InGaAs).
- Direct time-of-flight: photon timing → distance.
- Indirect time-of-flight: phase shift of modulated CW.
- Flash + scanning systems.

**Scientific spectroscopy**:
- Cooled CCD/CMOS for visible.
- InGaAs array for SWIR.
- HgCdTe for mid-IR.
- Bolometer / thermopile for far-IR / THz.

**Single-photon (quantum, astronomy)**:
- Si SPAD for visible (η~70%).
- SNSPD for telecom (η~95%) — best efficiency + low timing jitter.
- TES (transition-edge sensor): photon-number resolving.

**X-ray / gamma**:
- Si + Ge for X-ray spectroscopy (NDA-controlled).
- HPGe (high-purity Ge) for high-resolution gamma.
- Sodium iodide + LSO for radiation therapy + PET.

**Mid + far-IR**:
- HgCdTe (cooled).
- InSb (cooled).
- Microbolometer arrays (uncooled): FLIR thermal cameras.

**Specialized**:
- **PMT**: large-area + fast; scintillator + Cherenkov; legacy.
- **Streak camera**: ultrafast (~ps timing) imaging.
- **Spectrograph + CCD**: standard for spectral measurements.

question.question: Compute SNR for a Si photodiode receiver
question.goal: A Si PIN photodiode at 850 nm sees 1 µW optical power; responsivity 0.55 A/W; load resistor 50 Ω; T = 300 K; bandwidth 100 MHz; dark current 1 nA.

steps.reveal: Thermal dominates (182 nA >> 13.3 nA). Total noise ≈ 182 nA. SNR = 550 / 182 ≈ 3.0 → ~10 dB SNR. Limited by thermal in 50 Ω load + 100 MHz BW. To improve: cool detector (negligible at 300 K vs cryo); use transimpedance amp with low input-referred current noise; switch to APD with internal gain (improves SNR despite multiplication noise); raise load resistance (slower bandwidth). For DC + low-bandwidth: shot-noise-limited at this signal level.

question.question: Drag to the typical responsivity (in A/W) of a Si photodiode at 850 nm.
question.explanation: Si photodiode at 850 nm: responsivity ~0.5-0.6 A/W (η ~75-90%). Theoretical max R = e/(hν) = 0.68 A/W at 850 nm. For comparison: Ge at 1550 nm ~0.8 A/W (lower bandgap); InGaAs at 1550 nm ~0.8-1.0 A/W. PMT effective responsivity 10⁵-10⁶ A/W (high gain) but only ~30% QE at peak.

question.question: Match each detector to its primary application domain.
question.explanation:
Detector selection by application:
• **Visible imaging**: CMOS for cameras + smartphones (cheap, low-power, megapixel); CCD for scientific (low-noise, high-QE).
• **Telecom**: PIN photodiodes (Ge, InGaAs) for short reach; APDs for long-reach; balanced photodetectors + 90° hybrids for coherent.
• **Single-photon / low-light**: SPADs (Si, InGaAs for telecom); SNSPDs (best efficiency, cryogenic); SiPMs (large-area integrated SPADs); PMTs (legacy, still in particle physics).
• **Thermal / mid-IR**: microbolometers (uncooled, FLIR); HgCdTe + InSb (cooled, scientific + military).

Each combines: spectral range + speed + sensitivity + cost + size. Photonics-engineering choice is multi-dimensional. Modern trend: photonic-integrated detectors on Si or SiN + monolithic with electronics → low-cost integration.

question.question: Why have SPADs (single-photon avalanche diodes) become foundational for LIDAR + quantum?
options: SPADs detect single photons with ~ps timing resolution + Geiger-mode operation (avalanche fires on any photon). Used in time-of-flight LIDAR (autonomous-vehicle range), TCSPC (fluorescence lifetime imaging), quantum cryptography (BB84), quantum networking. Recent: large SPAD arrays (Sony IMX459/479 LIDAR sensors with thousands of SPADs); Si SPAD efficiency ~70%; InGaAs SPAD for telecom-wavelength quantum.
question.explanation:
**SPADs (Single-Photon Avalanche Diodes)**:

*Operation*: photodiode biased above breakdown (Geiger mode). Single absorbed photon → avalanche → mA-level pulse. Quenching circuit resets after each detection.

*Key specs*:
- **Photon Detection Efficiency (PDE)**: 30-70% (Si, 500-900 nm); 10-30% (InGaAs, 1550 nm); 95%+ (SNSPD, cryogenic).
- **Timing jitter**: 20-200 ps (Si SPAD); 50-100 ps (InGaAs); <10 ps (SNSPD).
- **Dark count rate (DCR)**: 10-1000 cps (Si); 1000-10⁴ cps (InGaAs); <1 cps (SNSPD).
- **Afterpulsing**: probability of false counts following an avalanche; lower-resolution timer of SPAD count rate.

*Applications*:

1. **LIDAR**: time-of-flight photon ranging.
   - Direct ToF: send pulse, measure return time; resolution ~3 mm/100 ps.
   - Indirect ToF: phase shift of modulated signal.
   - Sony IMX459 (2021): 256×189 SPAD array for automotive lidar.
   - Apple iPad Pro + iPhone Pro: SPAD-based LiDAR for AR/depth.
   - Solid-state automotive lidar (Velodyne, Innoviz, Aeva, Luminar): SPAD or APD + CMOS.

2. **Quantum cryptography**:
   - BB84 + variants: receive single photons in 2 polarization bases.
   - QKD networks: city-scale (Tokyo, Vienna, China backbone) + satellite (Micius 2017).
   - SPADs at 850 nm (Si) or 1550 nm (InGaAs) depending on link.

3. **Fluorescence-lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM)**:
   - TCSPC (time-correlated single-photon counting).
   - Determine fluorophore lifetime → distinguish bound/unbound state, microenvironment.

4. **Time-of-flight 3D imaging**:
   - Gating + sub-cm range resolution.
   - Indoor scene reconstruction, biomedical.

5. **Particle physics + biology**:
   - Cherenkov detectors.
   - DNA sequencing (Nanopore + PacBio use photon-counting variants).

6. **Quantum networking + computing**:
   - Photonic qubit detection.
   - Bell-state measurements + entanglement-swapping.

7. **Astronomy**:
   - Faint-target imaging.
   - Lucky-imaging post-processing.

*Recent advances*:
- **CMOS SPAD arrays**: monolithic 256×256+ on standard 65nm/40nm/28nm CMOS; cheap + scalable.
- **InGaAs SPAD arrays**: 32×32 + bigger emerging; cooled to suppress dark counts.
- **Free-running operation**: traditional gated; new TDM-quenched variants for arrays.
- **Time-skew correction**: digital calibration of per-pixel timing offsets.
- **3D-stacking**: optical SPAD die + CMOS readout die (Sony, ams).

*Limits*:
- Geometric fill factor: SPAD active region only ~10-30% of pixel area.
- Dark counts limit sensitivity; cooling helps.
- Afterpulsing.
- Saturation at high photon rates.

*Future*:
- Megapixel SPAD arrays (research direction).
- Higher-fill-factor designs.
- Compatible with CMOS processes for cheaper manufacturing.
- Integration with timing electronics + ML for noise reduction.

SPAD + SNSPD have re-enabled photon-counting at scale; foundation of modern quantum + lidar industries.

slides.workedSolution: SPADs (Geiger-mode avalanche photodiodes): single-photon detection with ps timing resolution. PDE 30-70% (Si), 10-30% (InGaAs), 95%+ (SNSPD cryo). Applications: LIDAR (automotive, AR/depth sensors), TCSPC + FLIM, quantum cryptography (BB84, QKD), time-of-flight 3D, particle physics, astronomy, quantum networking. CMOS SPAD arrays (Sony IMX459, Apple LiDAR) enable mass deployment. Limits: dark counts, afterpulsing, fill factor; future: megapixel + higher efficiency + cheaper manufacturing.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why photodetector noise + sensitivity ultimately limit how far + fast + low-light optical communications + sensing can go.
question.rubric: Mentions: any photodetector adds shot + thermal + dark + amplifier noise. Shot noise (∝ √I) is fundamental; cannot be reduced. Total noise determines minimum detectable signal — limits range (fiber spans, lidar range, telescope sensitivity), bandwidth (faster needs lower noise per Hz), low-light scenarios (single-photon counting, faint-object imaging, biomedical). Modern engineering: cool detector (reduce dark + thermal); use APD/SPAD/SNSPD (internal gain or photon-counting); design TIA with sub-pA/√Hz current noise; use coherent detection (LO heterodyne to shot-noise limit). Limits: deep-space optical (~10⁻¹⁸ W/m²), single-photon QKD (Bell experiments), low-light biomedical (10-100 photons per pixel imaging). Hardware + protocol co-evolution: every dB of detector improvement enables longer reach + faster rate. Concludes: photodetector engineering is invisible foundation of every optical system.
